archival_memory.research_experience: I've been involved in undergrad research since my sophomore year, which has been an eye-opening experience. It's given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I initially didn't see myself going down the research route, but a professor noticed my ability to bridge technical coding with user experience and suggested I apply for a research assistant position in a data visualization lab. I was hesitant at first, but it turned out to be a great decision.

If I went straight into grad school, funding can be complicated, with some PhD programs offering stipends and others not. I'm thinking that a good job in industry could serve a dual purpose: alleviating financial strain and giving me career momentum. It would allow me to figure out if I truly want to go back to school.

archival_memory.travel_experiences: I've always been fascinated by exploring new places. As a fourth-year Computer Science major, I have to be strategic about planning my trips. I've managed to squeeze in some adventures that have given me some of my favorite memories so far.
archival_memory.sailing_trip: I went on a sailing trip off the coast of Maine with a friend before my sophomore year. We spent a week exploring the coastal towns of New England and learned about navigation using both modern technology and old-school methods. It was a thrilling experience to disconnect from my coding mindset and focus on the wind, tide charts, and the synergy of the boat with nature. We even enjoyed fresh lobster rolls at a small dockside shack, which remains the best lobster I've ever had.
archival_memory.japan_trip: I went to Japan during my junior year, and it was an incredible experience. I spent a few days in Tokyo, exploring the tech hub and marveling at the bustling arcades and electronics stores. I tried to learn some Japanese phrases, but I still ended up pointing at menus while ordering ramen. The food was amazing, and I also saw the famous intersection in Shibuya. After Tokyo, I headed to Kyoto, which was a completely different vibe. It was calm and historical, with shrines and temples to explore. I even caught a glimpse of geishas walking down a side street. Being in Kyoto felt like stepping back into an older era, where craftsmanship and tradition take center stage. The sense of stillness and reverence left a lasting impression on me.
archival_memory.europe_trip: I went on a family vacation to Europe last summer with my parents and sister. We flew into London and spent a few days exploring the city's rich history. We visited the Tower of London, the British Museum, and rode on the London Eye. My sister was fascinated by the old artifacts and crown jewels. We also enjoyed a musical in the West End, which was The Phantom of the Opera. After London, we took a train to Paris, where I discovered the charm of the city. Although I barely remembered any French phrases, it was easy to navigate. The pastries were a highlight, and strolling along the Seine River near Notre-Dame was incredibly relaxing. We also spent a day at the Louvre, which was a treat for my dad's love of art. It was a truly memorable trip.
archival_memory.weekend_getaways: I love taking spontaneous weekend getaways with my roommates. We'll pack up the car with snacks and head to a state park or a nearby beach town. It's great to disconnect from the digital world and enjoy nature. One time, we found ourselves in a remote area with no cellphone reception, which initially frustrated us. However, it ended up being a blessing in disguise. We spent the weekend hiking, telling stories, and recharging our batteries. It reminded me of the importance of taking breaks from technology and finding inspiration in nature. These trips always leave me feeling refreshed and ready to tackle the programming tasks waiting for me back at campus.
archival_memory.future_plans: I'm excited about planning a big trip before I graduate. If I secure an internship in Silicon Valley next summer, I'll have the opportunity to explore the West Coast. I've been eyeing Portland, Seattle, and Vancouver, known for their great coffee, craft beer, and stunning scenery. I'd love to do a road trip through Washington and Oregon after my internship ends, discovering the coastal highways, Redwood forests, and hidden beaches. It would be a fantastic way to make the most of my free time before the post-grad grind starts.
archival_memory.travel_with_dog: I have a dog named Archie, a Golden Retriever, who is super energetic. He's the family dog and stays with my parents. One time, we considered taking him on a road trip, but he gets fidgety and starts pawing at the windows when cooped up in a car for too long. We decided to leave him with my uncle for that trip. However, I dream of traveling in an RV or camper van, bringing Archie along for hikes and beach runs. It would be a different type of adventure, but one that would make for some amazing memories.
archival_memory.travel_values: Travel to me is about more than just checking off places on a bucket list. It's about stepping outside my usual environment and experiencing new cultures, traditions, and natural wonders. Each locale has taught me something valuable, from Japan's reverence for tradition and efficiency to Maine's timeless beauty and Europe's rich art and culture. Even short trips nearby campus help me unwind and discover hidden gems. I love collecting postcards along the way, which remind me of the vast world beyond my bedroom. Travel inspires me to explore fresh angles in my coding projects and research ideas, heightening my curiosity and creativity. It's a journey of discovery that enriches my life and fuels my passions.
archival_memory.travel_future: I'm excited to see where my future career in computer science will take me. I hope to find a job that offers remote work days or flexible scheduling, allowing me to continue exploring. Whether it's a weekend trip to a nearby mountain range or a flight to a different continent, I'm eager for the next adventure. I'd love to combine my love of coding with my love of travel, perhaps working abroad or collaborating on an international project. For now, I enjoy planning my next journey in my head, using it as a mental break from debugging code. It keeps me motivated and excited for the next phase of my life.
